# unsafe-libyaml-norway 0.2.15 - Docs.rs

Source: https://docs.rs/crate/unsafe-libyaml-norway/latest

# unsafe-libyaml-norway

This library is [libyaml](https://github.com/yaml/libyaml/tree/2c891fc7a770e8ba2fec34fc6b545c672beb37e6) translated from C to unsafe Rust with the assistance
of [c2rust](https://github.com/immunant/c2rust).

```
[]
 = "0.2"
```
*Compiler support: requires rustc 1.60+*

## License

MIT license, same as libyaml.

---

# unsafe-libyaml-norway 0.2.15 - Docs.rs

Source: https://docs.rs/crate/unsafe-libyaml-norway/latest/source/

#
                    unsafe-libyaml-norway 0.2.15

                libyaml transpiled to rust by c2rust

---

# pretty_assertions - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/pretty_assertions/^1.0/

## Expand description

[§](https://docs.rs#pretty-assertions)Pretty Assertions

When writing tests in Rust, you’ll probably use `assert_eq!(a, b)` *a lot*.

If such a test fails, it will present all the details of `a` and `b`.
But you have to spot the differences yourself, which is not always straightforward,
like here:

Wouldn’t that task be *much* easier with a colorful diff?

Yep — and you only need **one line of code** to make it happen:

`use pretty_assertions::{assert_eq, assert_ne};`## Show the example behind the screenshots above.

[ⓘ](https://docs.rs)

```
// 1. add the `pretty_assertions` dependency to `Cargo.toml`.
// 2. insert this line at the top of each module, as needed
use pretty_assertions::{assert_eq, assert_ne};
#[derive(Debug, PartialEq)]
struct Foo {
    lorem: &'static str,
    ipsum: u32,
    dolor: Result<String, String>,
}
let x = Some(Foo { lorem: "Hello World!", ipsum: 42, dolor: Ok("hey".to_string())});
let y = Some(Foo { lorem: "Hello Wrold!", ipsum: 42, dolor: Ok("hey ho!".to_string())});
assert_eq!(x, y);
```
[§](https://docs.rs#tip)Tip

Specify it as [ [dev-dependencies]](http://doc.crates.io/specifying-dependencies.html#development-dependencies)
and it will only be used for compiling tests, examples, and benchmarks.
This way the compile time of

`cargo build` won’t be affected!Also add `#[cfg(test)]` to your `use` statements, like this:

```
#[cfg(test)]
use pretty_assertions::{assert_eq, assert_ne};
```
[§](https://docs.rs#note)Note

- Since `Rust 2018`edition, you need to declare`use pretty_assertions::{assert_eq, assert_ne};`per module. Before you would write`#[macro_use] extern crate pretty_assertions;`.
- The replacement is only effective in your own crate, not in other libraries you include.
- `assert_ne`is also switched to multi-line presentation, but does- *not*show a diff.

[§](https://docs.rs#features)Features

Features provided by the crate are:

- `std`: Use the Rust standard library. Enabled by default. Exactly one of- `std`and- `alloc`is required.
- `alloc`: Use the- `alloc`crate. Exactly one of- `std`and- `alloc`is required.
- `unstable`: opt-in to unstable features that may not follow Semantic Versioning. The implementation behind this feature is subject to change without warning between patch versions.

## Macros[§](https://docs.rs#macros)

- [assert_](https://docs.rs/macro.assert_eq.html)- eq
- Asserts that two expressions are equal to each other (using `PartialEq`
- [assert_](https://docs.rs/macro.assert_matches.html)- matches
- Asserts that a value matches a pattern.
- [assert_](https://docs.rs/macro.assert_ne.html)- ne
- Asserts that two expressions are not equal to each other (using `PartialEq`
- [assert_](https://docs.rs/macro.assert_str_eq.html)- str_ - eq
- Asserts that two expressions are equal to each other (using `PartialEq`

## Structs[§](https://docs.rs#structs)

- [Comparison](https://docs.rs/struct.Comparison.html)
- A comparison of two values.
- [StrComparison](https://docs.rs/struct.StrComparison.html)
- A comparison of two strings.

---

# About Docs.rs

Source: https://docs.rs/about

Docs.rs is an
            [open source](https://github.com/rust-lang/docs.rs)
            documentation host for crates of the
            [Rust Programming Language](https://www.rust-lang.org/).
            All libraries published to [crates.io](https://crates.io)
            are documented. If you just published a crate, your crate is likely
            still in [the queue](https://docs.rs/releases/queue).

            The source code of Docs.rs is available on
            [GitHub](https://github.com/rust-lang/docs.rs). If
            you ever encounter an issue, don't hesitate to report it! (And
            thanks in advance!)

Currently running Docs.rs version is: **0.0.0 (964c90a45859fd8f9076e3cbe58470a5a4f4d4f7 2026-07-01 )**

Summaries of the documentation build processes [are available at /releases/](https://docs.rs/releases).

            JavaScript in support of documentation is allowed but not guaranteed to work on docs.rs. What that
            means: If you write documentation that inlines some JavaScript (like
            [KaTeX](https://katex.org/)), that's allowed, and
            will probably work today but may break in the future.

However, it's not allowed to put JavaScript or other content in docs published on docs.rs for the purpose of tracking visitors. For instance, adding Google Analytics scripts, tracking pixels, or site verification for services like Google Search Console. Crates that do this will have the relevant versions removed and may be blocked from docs.rs.

            Docs.rs is run and maintained by the [Docs.rs team](https://www.rust-lang.org/governance/teams/dev-tools#team-docs-rs).
            You can find us in #t-docs-rs on [Zulip](https://rust-lang.zulipchat.com/#narrow/stream/356853-t-docs-rs).

---

# Badges

Source: https://docs.rs/about/badges

Docs.rs no longer has its own badges. Consider using [shields.io](https://shields.io) instead.

---

# Builds

Source: https://docs.rs/about/builds

Docs.rs automatically builds documentation for crates released on [crates.io](https://crates.io/).
                It may take a while to build your crate, depending on how many crates are in [the queue](https://docs.rs/releases/queue).

                All crates are built in a sandbox using the nightly release of the Rust compiler.
                The current version in use is `rustc 1.98.0-nightly (c397dae80 2026-07-02)`.

                The README displayed on docs.rs follows Cargo’s `package.readme` rules.
                If `readme` is not set, docs.rs will look for `README.md`, `README.txt`, or `README` in the crate root.
                Set `readme = "path/to/file"` to use a custom file, `readme = true` to use `README.md`, or `readme = false` to disable the README.

                To recognize Docs.rs from your Rust code, you can test for the `docsrs` cfg, e.g.:

```
```
                To recognize Docs.rs from `build.rs` files, you can test for the environment variable `DOCS_RS`, e.g.:

`if var.is_ok `
              All targets other than `x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu` are cross-compiled. For implementation reasons, this is unlikely to change for the foreseeable future.

                You can configure how your crate is built by adding [package metadata](https://docs.rs/metadata) to your `Cargo.toml`, e.g.:

```
[]
 = ["--cfg", "my_cfg"]
```
`#[cfg(my_cfg)]` (not to be confused with `#[cfg(doc)]`) can be used for conditional compilation.
                This approach is also useful for setting
                When you start using docs.rs metadata or `#[cfg(docsrs)]` in your code, you might run into issues
                where your code builds fine locally but fails on docs.rs.
                To avoid this, you can add [ cargo docs-rs](https://github.com/dtolnay/cargo-docs-rs) to
                your test-suite.
                While it doesn't perfectly replicate our build environment, it can catch many common issues.

                The Docs.rs [README](https://github.com/rust-lang/docs.rs/blob/master/README.md#build-subcommand) describes how to build
                unpublished crate documentation locally using the same build environment as the Docs.rs build agent.

                Missing dependencies are a common reason for failed builds.
                Docs.rs dependencies are managed through
                [crates-build-env](https://github.com/rust-lang/crates-build-env).
                See [Forge](https://forge.rust-lang.org/docs-rs/add-dependencies.html) for how to add a dependency.

                Most of the sandbox is a read-only file system, including the source directory of your crate and its dependencies.
                If your `build.rs` generates files that are relevant for documentation, consider writing to the
                [cargo output directory](https://doc.rust-lang.org/cargo/reference/environment-variables.html#environment-variables-cargo-sets-for-crates),
                passed in the environment variable `OUT_DIR`.

All the builds are executed inside a sandbox with limited resources. The current limits are:

| Available RAM | 6.44 GB |
| Maximum rustdoc execution time | 15m |
| Maximum size of a build log | 102.4 kB |
| Network access | blocked |
| Maximum number of build targets | 10 |

                If your build fails because it hit one of these limits, please
                [open an issue](https://github.com/rust-lang/docs.rs/issues/new/choose)
                to get them increased for your crate.
                Since our build agent has finite resources, we have to consider each case individually. However, there are a few general policies:

If your crate fails to build for a reason not listed here, you can rebuild it from [crates.io](https://crates.io) website as you can see below:

Or you can [file an issue](https://github.com/rust-lang/docs.rs/issues) if you think it's a **docs.rs** issue.

---

# Metadata

Source: https://docs.rs/about/metadata

You can customize docs.rs builds by defining `[package.metadata.docs.rs]`
		table in your crates' `Cargo.toml`.

The available configuration flags you can customize are:

```
[]
 = "test"
[]
# Features to pass to Cargo (default: [])
 = ["feature1", "feature2"]
# Whether to pass `--all-features` to Cargo (default: false)
 = true
# Whether to pass `--no-default-features` to Cargo (default: false)
 = true
# Target to test build on, used as the default landing page (default: "x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu")
#
# Any target supported by rustup can be used.
 = "x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu"
# Targets to build (default: see below)
#
# Any target supported by rustup can be used.
#
# Default targets:
# - x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu
# - aarch64-apple-darwin
# - x86_64-pc-windows-msvc
# - aarch64-unknown-linux-gnu
# - i686-pc-windows-msvc
#
# Set this to `[]` to only build the default target.
#
# If `default-target` is unset, the first element of `targets` is treated as the default target.
# Otherwise, these `targets` are built in addition to the default target.
# If both `default-target` and `targets` are unset,
#   all tier-one targets will be built and `x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu` will be used as the default target.
 = ["aarch64-apple-darwin", "x86_64-pc-windows-msvc"]
# If you want to instead add another target without overwriting the default ones:
 = ["i686-apple-darwin"]
# Additional `RUSTFLAGS` to set (default: [])
 = ["--example-rustc-arg"]
# Additional `RUSTDOCFLAGS` to set (default: [])
 = ["--example-rustdoc-arg"]
# List of command line arguments for `cargo`.
#
# These cannot be a subcommand, they may only be options.
 = ["-Z", "build-std"]
```

---

# Shorthand URLs

Source: https://docs.rs/about/redirections

Docs.rs uses semver to parse URLs. You can use this feature to access
            crates' documentation easily. Example of URL redirections for
            `clap` crate:

| URL | Redirects to documentation of |
|---|---|
| [docs.rs/clap](https://docs.rs/clap) | Latest version of clap |
| [docs.rs/clap::Command](https://docs.rs/clap::Command) | Latest version of clap, and search for "Command" within the crate |
| [docs.rs/clap/~2](https://docs.rs/clap/%7E2) | 2.* version |
| [docs.rs/clap/~2.9](https://docs.rs/clap/%7E2.9) | 2.9.* version |
| [docs.rs/clap/2.9.3](https://docs.rs/clap/2.9.3) | 2.9.3 version (you don't need `=`unlike semver) |
| [docs.rs/clap/*](https://docs.rs/clap/*) | Latest version of this page (if it still exists). "latest" or "newest" work as well as `*`. |

---

# Download

Source: https://docs.rs/about/download

docs.rs stores the `rustdoc` output in a ZIP file.

                These archives can be used as a base for further processing of
                the documentation for offline readers like Dash or Zeal.
                **They are not directly usable for offline documentation.**

The download is possible for specific or semantic versions:

But also viaTo unpack the ZIP file you need any zip utility that supports PKZIP version 4.6 and BZIP2 & Deflate compression.

The archives will contain all the documentation HTML files for all targets and CSS/JS assets that are specific to the build. The default target will be found at the root, and other targets each in its own subfolder.

                Docs.rs is running rustdoc with `--static-root-path "/-/rustdoc.static/"`,
                which leads to all references to static assets breaking if they are not
                available under that path. Older builds used `--static-root-path "/"`, which
                means you will have to handle both.

                Since we're also adding `--emit=invocation-specific` to our build
                the archives will *not* contain any static assets that are specific to the
                toolchain. For now these will have to be downloaded file-by-file directly
                from docs.rs.

---

# Rustdoc JSON

Source: https://docs.rs/about/rustdoc-json

docs.rs builds & hosts the [ rustdoc JSON](https://doc.rust-lang.org/rustdoc/unstable-features.html#json-output) output.

This structured version of the documentation can be used for inspecting the docs and types of the crate in a programmatic way.

                The JSON file you're downloading might have been built with an older version of `rustdoc`
                so you might have to check the `format_version` attribute to determine how to parse the structure.
                The [ rustdoc-types](https://docs.rs/rustdoc-types/) crate helps with this.

**
                We started building rustdoc JSON on 2025-05-23. So any release before that won't have a download
                available until our rebuilds reached that release.
            **

                The download URLs can be generic or specific, depending on what you need. In case of rebuilds we
                also keep old format versions around. **Until we rebuilt all releases, we might return
                a `404 NOT FOUND` for some.**

By default we use `zstd` compression, which is more space efficient and faster to decompress. For more limited environments we also started supporting `gzip` compression. You can receive gzip by adding `.gz` to the given URL.

Here some URL examples you can use.

| URL | Redirects to JSON download of |
|---|---|
| [https://docs.rs/crate/clap/latest/json](https://docs.rs/crate/clap/latest/json) | latest version, default target, latest format-version |
| [https://docs.rs/crate/clap/latest/json.gz](https://docs.rs/crate/clap/latest/json.gz) | latest version, default target, latest format-version, gzip compression |
| [https://docs.rs/crate/clap/latest/json/42](https://docs.rs/crate/clap/latest/json/42) | latest version, default target, format-version 42 |
| [https://docs.rs/crate/clap/~4/json](https://docs.rs/crate/clap/%7E4/json) | latest v4 via semver, default target, latest format-version |
| [https://docs.rs/crate/clap/~4/json.zst](https://docs.rs/crate/clap/%7E4/json.zst) | latest v4 via semver, default target, latest format-version, zstd compression |
| [https://docs.rs/crate/clap/latest/i686-pc-windows-msvc/json](https://docs.rs/crate/clap/latest/i686-pc-windows-msvc/json) | latest version, windows target, latest format-version |

---

# sim_lib_midi_sysex - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/sim-lib-midi-sysex/0.1.0-rc.1/sim_lib_midi_sysex/

## Expand description

Typed views over MIDI system-exclusive (SysEx) messages.

This crate interprets the opaque byte payload of a
[ SysExEvent](https://docs.rs/sim-lib-midi-core/0.1.0-rc.1/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/sim_lib_midi_core/model/enum.SysExEvent.html) as structured messages and
serialises them back. It covers Universal SysEx (

[) and the MIDI Tuning Standard (](https://docs.rs/struct.UniversalSysEx.html)

`UniversalSysEx`[), plus Yamaha manufacturer SysEx (](https://docs.rs/struct.MtsMessage.html)

`MtsMessage`[) and the DX7 voice/bank patch formats (](https://docs.rs/struct.YamahaSysEx.html)

`YamahaSysEx`[,](https://docs.rs/enum.Dx7Bulk.html)

`Dx7Bulk`[,](https://docs.rs/struct.Dx7Voice.html)

`Dx7Voice`[,](https://docs.rs/struct.Dx7VoiceBank.html)

`Dx7VoiceBank`[,](https://docs.rs/struct.Dx7Operator.html)

`Dx7Operator`[), including packed/unpacked voice conversion and Yamaha checksums. All data bytes are validated as 7-bit; failures surface as](https://docs.rs/struct.Dx7VoiceCommon.html)

`Dx7VoiceCommon`[.](https://docs.rs/enum.SysExViewError.html)

`SysExViewError`[§](https://docs.rs#examples)Examples

Round-tripping a Universal SysEx message through its `F0` payload:

```
use sim_lib_midi_sysex::{UniversalRealm, UniversalSysEx};
let message = UniversalSysEx::new(
    UniversalRealm::NonRealTime,
    0x7f,
    0x08,
    0x01,
    vec![0x00, 0x12],
)
.unwrap();
let payload = message.to_f0_payload().unwrap();
assert_eq!(UniversalSysEx::from_f0_payload(&payload).unwrap(), message);
```
## Structs[§](https://docs.rs#structs)

- [Dx7Operator](https://docs.rs/struct.Dx7Operator.html)
- One DX7 operator’s decoded envelope and oscillator parameters.
- [Dx7Voice](https://docs.rs/struct.Dx7Voice.html)
- A single DX7 voice, stored as its unpacked edit buffer with the original packed bytes retained when it was parsed from a bank.
- [Dx7Voice](https://docs.rs/struct.Dx7VoiceBank.html)- Bank
- A DX7 bank of 32 voices, retaining the raw packed bytes it was parsed from.
- [Dx7Voice](https://docs.rs/struct.Dx7VoiceCommon.html)- Common
- The voice-wide DX7 parameters shared across operators.
- [MtsMessage](https://docs.rs/struct.MtsMessage.html)
- A MIDI Tuning Standard message: a `UniversalSysEx`
- [Universal](https://docs.rs/struct.UniversalSysEx.html)- SysEx
- A parsed Universal SysEx message (realm, device id, two sub-ids, payload).
- [Yamaha](https://docs.rs/struct.YamahaSysEx.html)- SysEx
- A parsed Yamaha SysEx message body (sub-status, format, and data, framed by the manufacturer id, byte count, and checksum).

## Enums[§](https://docs.rs#enums)

- [Dx7Bulk](https://docs.rs/enum.Dx7Bulk.html)
- A DX7 bulk-dump message: either a single voice or a full bank.
- [MtsMessage](https://docs.rs/enum.MtsMessageKind.html)- Kind
- The kind of MIDI Tuning Standard message, keyed by sub-id 2.
- [SysEx](https://docs.rs/enum.SysExViewError.html)- View - Error
- Errors raised while interpreting or building typed SysEx views.
- [Universal](https://docs.rs/enum.UniversalRealm.html)- Realm
- Which Universal SysEx realm a message belongs to.

## Constants[§](https://docs.rs#constants)

- [DX7_](https://docs.rs/constant.DX7_BANK_BYTE_COUNT.html)- BANK_ - BYTE_ - COUNT
- Total bytes of a packed DX7 bank.
- [DX7_](https://docs.rs/constant.DX7_BANK_VOICE_COUNT.html)- BANK_ - VOICE_ - COUNT
- Number of voices in a DX7 bank.
- [DX7_](https://docs.rs/constant.DX7_OPERATOR_COUNT.html)- OPERATOR_ - COUNT
- Number of operators in a DX7 voice.
- [DX7_](https://docs.rs/constant.DX7_OPERATOR_EDIT_BYTE_COUNT.html)- OPERATOR_ - EDIT_ - BYTE_ - COUNT
- Bytes per operator in the unpacked (edit-buffer) layout.
- [DX7_](https://docs.rs/constant.DX7_OPERATOR_PACKED_BYTE_COUNT.html)- OPERATOR_ - PACKED_ - BYTE_ - COUNT
- Bytes per operator in the packed layout.
- [DX7_](https://docs.rs/constant.DX7_PACKED_VOICE_BYTE_COUNT.html)- PACKED_ - VOICE_ - BYTE_ - COUNT
- Total bytes of a packed voice.
- [DX7_](https://docs.rs/constant.DX7_SINGLE_VOICE_BYTE_COUNT.html)- SINGLE_ - VOICE_ - BYTE_ - COUNT
- Total bytes of an unpacked single voice.
- [DX7_](https://docs.rs/constant.DX7_SINGLE_VOICE_FORMAT.html)- SINGLE_ - VOICE_ - FORMAT
- DX7 format byte for a single (edit-buffer) voice (`0x00`).
- [DX7_](https://docs.rs/constant.DX7_VOICE_BANK_FORMAT.html)- VOICE_ - BANK_ - FORMAT
- DX7 format byte for a 32-voice bank (`0x09`).
- [MIDI_](https://docs.rs/constant.MIDI_TUNING_STANDARD_SUB_ID.html)- TUNING_ - STANDARD_ - SUB_ - ID
- Sub-id 1 identifying a MIDI Tuning Standard message (`0x08`).
- [UNIVERSAL_](https://docs.rs/constant.UNIVERSAL_NON_REAL_TIME_ID.html)- NON_ - REAL_ - TIME_ - ID
- Status id introducing a Universal Non-Real-Time SysEx message (`0x7e`).
- [UNIVERSAL_](https://docs.rs/constant.UNIVERSAL_REAL_TIME_ID.html)- REAL_ - TIME_ - ID
- Status id introducing a Universal Real-Time SysEx message (`0x7f`).
- [YAMAHA_](https://docs.rs/constant.YAMAHA_MANUFACTURER_ID.html)- MANUFACTURER_ - ID
- Yamaha’s MIDI manufacturer id (`0x43`).

## Functions[§](https://docs.rs#functions)

- [yamaha_](https://docs.rs/fn.yamaha_checksum.html)- checksum
- Computes the Yamaha SysEx checksum (two’s-complement of the 7-bit sum).

# wikrs - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/wikrs/0.2.0/wikrs/

## Expand description

**wikrs** — fast, honest wikitext extraction and parsing.

Turns MediaWiki wikitext (the markup inside Wikipedia XML dumps) into clean
plain text or a structured AST, and **emits a diagnostic when it hits input
it can’t faithfully handle instead of silently corrupting the output**.
Validated on the full English Wikipedia (7.19M articles, 98.0% of pages
convert with zero residual markup).

[§](https://docs.rs#quick-start)Quick start

```
// Parse wikitext into an AST + diagnostics, then render plain text.
let parsed = wikrs::parser::parse("'''Earth''' is a [[Planet|planet]].");
assert!(parsed.diagnostics.is_empty());
assert_eq!(wikrs::render::plain(&parsed.nodes), "Earth is a planet.");
// Or the Stage 1 one-shot stripper (fast, lossy, no diagnostics).
assert_eq!(
    wikrs::extract::strip("'''Earth''' is a [[Planet|planet]]."),
    "Earth is a planet."
);
```
Reading a whole dump ([ dump::open](https://docs.rs/dump/fn.open.html), or

[for parallel bz2 decoding) yields](https://docs.rs/dump/fn.open_multistream.html)

`dump::open_multistream`[s whose](https://docs.rs/dump/struct.Page.html)

`dump::Page``text` feeds the same
two entry points. The `wikrs` CLI wraps exactly this pipeline.Pre-1.0: the API surface is the modules documented below; items marked
`#[doc(hidden)]` are internal plumbing with no stability promise.

## Modules[§](https://docs.rs#modules)

- [ast](https://docs.rs/ast/index.html)
- The wikitext AST (Stage 2).
- [diag](https://docs.rs/diag/index.html)
- Diagnostics (DESIGN.md §7). The engine’s honesty mechanism: when it meets a
construct outside the declared support range, it emits an `Unsupported`diagnostic with the original source span — instead of silently producing something plausible but wrong.
- [dump](https://docs.rs/dump/index.html)
- Streaming reader for Wikimedia XML dumps (`pages-articles-multistream.xml.bz2`).
- [extract](https://docs.rs/extract/index.html)
- Stage 1: lossy `wikitext -> plain text`extraction.
- [parser](https://docs.rs/parser/index.html)
- Parser: wikitext → AST + diagnostics, over a deliberately small but honest
subset (paragraphs, headings, bold/italic, links, nested & definition lists,
refs/nowiki/comments, inline HTML formatting, preformatted). Inline templates
are dropped with a `W-TEMPLATE`warning (we don’t expand them — that would sacrifice the speed that is the whole point); tables and structural HTML become`Node::Unsupported`
- [render](https://docs.rs/render/index.html)
- Render an AST to output. Stage 2 starts with plain text — the same product
as Stage 1’s `extract::strip`, but driven by a real parse so it can preserve structure. Structured (JSONL) and HTML renderers come later.

---

# cu_safetymon - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/cu-safetymon/1.0.0/cu_safetymon/

## Expand description

Safety monitor for fault latching and fail-fast process termination.

`CuSafetyMon` is designed for safety-critical deployments where “keep running”
is less important than deterministic fault containment.

Behavior:

- Maintains a CopperList heartbeat (`process_copperlist`) and exits if no progress is observed within`copperlist_deadline_ms`.
- Consumes the runtime execution probe to report the last known
`(component_id, step, culistid)`when a lock is detected.
- Registers with Copper’s shared panic hook and turns panics into explicit process exit codes.
- Latches runtime errors (`process_error`) as shutdown faults with their own exit code. The`process_error`index is a monitored component index into`CuMonitoringMetadata::components()`.

Config (monitor `config` map keys):

- `copperlist_deadline_ms`(u64, default: 1000)
- `watchdog_period_ms`(u64, default:- `max(deadline/4, 10)`)
- `exit_code_shutdown`(i32, default: 70)
- `exit_code_lock`(i32, default: 71)
- `exit_code_panic`(i32, default: 72)

Implementation is split by target profile:

- `std_impl`: full watchdog/panic/exit behavior.
- `nostd_impl`: compile-only placeholder (behavior intentionally deferred).

---

## Expand description

Lightweight Copper monitor that periodically dumps compact runtime stats over the
standard `debug!` / `info!` logging macros.

# re_gamepad - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/re_gamepad/0.34.0-rc.4/re_gamepad/

## Expand description

Gamepad input handling for the Rerun viewer.

The crate keeps device polling separate from view-specific camera behavior.

Its default mapping uses a conventional dual-stick gamepad layout and returns 3D navigation intents in Rerun’s RUB view space.

## Structs[§](https://docs.rs#structs)

- [Gamepad](https://docs.rs/struct.GamepadInput.html)- Input
- Raw, device-independent gamepad input used by the standard mapping.
- [Gamepad](https://docs.rs/struct.GamepadManager.html)- Manager
- Native gamepad manager backed by `gilrs`.
- [Gamepad](https://docs.rs/struct.GamepadNavigation.html)- Navigation
- Mapped navigation command for a 3D view.
- [Standard](https://docs.rs/struct.StandardGamepadMapping.html)- Gamepad - Mapping
- Standard dual-stick mapping from raw gamepad input to 3D navigation.

## Functions[§](https://docs.rs#functions)

- [clear_](https://docs.rs/fn.clear_event_waker.html)- event_ - waker
- Clears the gamepad event callback and parks the backend until it is enabled again.
- [navigation_](https://docs.rs/fn.navigation_from_active_gamepad.html)- from_ - active_ - gamepad
- Polls the active gamepad and maps it to a navigation command.
- [set_](https://docs.rs/fn.set_event_waker.html)- event_ - waker
- Registers a callback that is called whenever the gamepad backend observes input.

# camel_component_wasm - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/camel-component-wasm/0.22.0/camel_component_wasm/

## Expand description

WebAssembly component for rust-camel — executes WASM modules as route processors via a Wasmtime runtime.

Main types: `WasmComponent`, `WasmBundle`, `WasmConfig`, `WasmEndpoint`, `StateStore`.
Main modules: `runtime`, `bindings`, `state_store`, `host_functions`.

[§](https://docs.rs#limitations)Limitations

- Only the [Wasmtime](https://wasmtime.dev)runtime is supported; other WASM runtimes (Wasmer, WasmEdge, etc.) are not compatible.
- WASM modules must export a specific interface defined by `camel_wasm_bindings`; arbitrary WASM binaries cannot be dropped in without meeting this contract.
- The WASM sandbox has no access to the host filesystem or network by default;
host functions are limited to what is explicitly exposed via `host_functions`.
- Epoch-based fuel/interruption requires the `epoch`feature; long-running modules without epoch support may block the async executor.

## Re-exports[§](https://docs.rs#reexports)

- `pub use authorization_policy::`- [WasmAuthorizationPolicyEvaluator](https://docs.rs/authorization_policy/struct.WasmAuthorizationPolicyEvaluator.html);
- `pub use authorization_policy::`- [build_permission_registry](https://docs.rs/authorization_policy/fn.build_permission_registry.html);
- `pub use bundle::`- [WasmBundle](https://docs.rs/bundle/struct.WasmBundle.html);
- `pub use config::`- [WasmConfig](https://docs.rs/config/struct.WasmConfig.html);
- `pub use endpoint::`- [WasmEndpoint](https://docs.rs/endpoint/struct.WasmEndpoint.html);
- `pub use epoch::`- [EpochTicker](https://docs.rs/epoch/struct.EpochTicker.html);
- `pub use error::`- [TrapReason](https://docs.rs/error/enum.TrapReason.html);
- `pub use error::`- [WasmError](https://docs.rs/error/enum.WasmError.html);

# unsafe-libyaml-norway

This library is [libyaml](https://github.com/yaml/libyaml/tree/2c891fc7a770e8ba2fec34fc6b545c672beb37e6) translated from C to unsafe Rust with the assistance
of [c2rust](https://github.com/immunant/c2rust).

```
[]
 = "0.2"
```
*Compiler support: requires rustc 1.60+*

## License

MIT license, same as libyaml.

[184](#184)    pub unsafe fn strncmp(
[185](#185)        lhs: *const [libc::c_char](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/primitive.i8.html),
[186](#186)        rhs: *const [libc::c_char](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/primitive.i8.html),
[187](#187)        mut count: [libc::c_ulong](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/primitive.u64.html),
[188](#188)    ) -> [libc::c_int](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/primitive.i32.html) {
[189](#189)        let mut lhs = [lhs](#185).[cast](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/ptr/foreigntype.const_ptr.html#method.cast)::<[u8](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/primitive.u8.html)>();
[190](#190)        let mut rhs = [rhs](#186).[cast](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/ptr/foreigntype.const_ptr.html#method.cast)::<[u8](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/primitive.u8.html)>();
[191](#191)        while count > 0 && *lhs != 0 && *lhs == *rhs {
[192](#192)            lhs = lhs.add(1);
[193](#193)            rhs = rhs.add(1);
[194](#194)            count -= 1;
[195](#195)        }
[196](#196)        if [count](#187) == 0 {
[197](#197)            0
[198](#198)        } else {
[199](#199)            (*[lhs](#189)).[cmp](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/cmp/trait.Ord.html#tymethod.cmp)(&*[rhs](#190)) as [libc::c_int](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/primitive.i32.html)
[200](#200)        }
[201](#201)    }

[203](#203)    macro_rules! __assert {
[204](#204)        (false $(,)?) => {
[205](#205)            $crate::externs::__assert_fail(stringify!(false), file!(), line!())
[206](#206)        };
[207](#207)        ($assertion:expr $(,)?) => {
[208](#208)            if !$assertion {
[209](#209)                $crate::externs::__assert_fail(stringify!($assertion), file!(), line!());
[210](#210)            }
[211](#211)        };
[212](#212)    }
[213](#213)
[214](#214)    pub(crate) unsafe fn __assert_fail(
[215](#215)        __assertion: &'static [str](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/primitive.str.html),
[216](#216)        __file: &'static [str](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/primitive.str.html),
[217](#217)        __line: [u32](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/primitive.u32.html),
[218](#218)    ) -> ! {
[219](#219)        struct Abort;
[220](#220)        impl [Drop](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/ops/drop/trait.Drop.html) for [Abort](#219) {
[221](#221)            fn drop(&mut self) {
[222](#222)                [panic!](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/macro.panic.html)();
[223](#223)            }
[224](#224)        }
[225](#225)        let _abort_on_panic = [Abort](#219);
[226](#226)        [panic!](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/macro.panic.html)("{}:{}: Assertion `{}` failed.", __file, __line, __assertion);
[227](#227)    }

```
union {
    /// The stream parameters (for YAML_STREAM_START_EVENT).
    stream_start: struct {
        /// The document encoding.
        encoding: yaml_encoding_t,
    },
    /// The document parameters (for YAML_DOCUMENT_START_EVENT).
    document_start: struct {
        /// The version directive.
        version_directive: *mut yaml_version_directive_t,
        /// The list of tag directives.
        tag_directives: struct {
            /// The beginning of the tag directives list.
            start: *mut yaml_tag_directive_t,
            /// The end of the tag directives list.
            end: *mut yaml_tag_directive_t,
        },
        /// Is the document indicator implicit?
        implicit: i32,
    },
    /// The document end parameters (for YAML_DOCUMENT_END_EVENT).
    document_end: struct {
        /// Is the document end indicator implicit?
        implicit: i32,
    },
    /// The alias parameters (for YAML_ALIAS_EVENT).
    alias: struct {
        /// The anchor.
        anchor: *mut u8,
    },
    /// The scalar parameters (for YAML_SCALAR_EVENT).
    scalar: struct {
        /// The anchor.
        anchor: *mut u8,
        /// The tag.
        tag: *mut u8,
        /// The scalar value.
        value: *mut u8,
        /// The length of the scalar value.
        length: u64,
        /// Is the tag optional for the plain style?
        plain_implicit: i32,
        /// Is the tag optional for any non-plain style?
        quoted_implicit: i32,
        /// The scalar style.
        style: yaml_scalar_style_t,
    },
    /// The sequence parameters (for YAML_SEQUENCE_START_EVENT).
    sequence_start: struct {
        /// The anchor.
        anchor: *mut u8,
        /// The tag.
        tag: *mut u8,
        /// Is the tag optional?
        implicit: i32,
        /// The sequence style.
        style: yaml_sequence_style_t,
    },
    /// The mapping parameters (for YAML_MAPPING_START_EVENT).
    mapping_start: struct {
        /// The anchor.
        anchor: *mut u8,
        /// The tag.
        tag: *mut u8,
        /// Is the tag optional?
        implicit: i32,
        /// The mapping style.
        style: yaml_mapping_style_t,
    },
}
```

        /// The tag suffix.

    },
    /// The scalar value (for YAML_SCALAR_TOKEN).

        /// The scalar style.
        style: yaml_scalar_style_t,
    },
    /// The version directive (for YAML_VERSION_DIRECTIVE_TOKEN).
    version_directive: struct {
        /// The major version number.
        major: i32,
        /// The minor version number.

    },

```
#[non_exhaustive]#[repr(u32)]pub enum yaml_break_t {
    YAML_ANY_BREAK = 0,
    YAML_CR_BREAK = 1,
    YAML_LN_BREAK = 2,
    YAML_CRLN_BREAK = 3,
}
```
## Expand description

Line break type.

## Variants (Non-exhaustive)[§](https://docs.rs#variants)

## This enum is marked as non-exhaustive

Non-exhaustive enums could have additional variants added in future. Therefore, when matching against variants of non-exhaustive enums, an extra wildcard arm must be added to account for any future variants.

[§](https://docs.rs#variant.YAML_ANY_BREAK)

### YAML_ANY_BREAK = 0

Let the parser choose the break type.

[§](https://docs.rs#variant.YAML_CR_BREAK)

### YAML_CR_BREAK = 1

Use CR for line breaks (Mac style).

[§](https://docs.rs#variant.YAML_LN_BREAK)

### YAML_LN_BREAK = 2

Use LN for line breaks (Unix style).

[§](https://docs.rs#variant.YAML_CRLN_BREAK)

### YAML_CRLN_BREAK = 3

Use CR LN for line breaks (DOS style).

# yaml_error_type_t in unsafe_libyaml_norway - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/unsafe-libyaml-norway/0.2.15/unsafe_libyaml_norway/enum.yaml_error_type_t.html

```
#[non_exhaustive]#[repr(u32)]pub enum yaml_error_type_t {
    YAML_NO_ERROR = 0,
    YAML_MEMORY_ERROR = 1,
    YAML_READER_ERROR = 2,
    YAML_SCANNER_ERROR = 3,
    YAML_PARSER_ERROR = 4,
    YAML_COMPOSER_ERROR = 5,
    YAML_WRITER_ERROR = 6,
    YAML_EMITTER_ERROR = 7,
}
```
## Expand description

Many bad things could happen with the parser and emitter.

## Variants (Non-exhaustive)[§](https://docs.rs#variants)

## This enum is marked as non-exhaustive

[§](https://docs.rs#variant.YAML_NO_ERROR)

### YAML_NO_ERROR = 0

No error is produced.

[§](https://docs.rs#variant.YAML_MEMORY_ERROR)

### YAML_MEMORY_ERROR = 1

Cannot allocate or reallocate a block of memory.

[§](https://docs.rs#variant.YAML_READER_ERROR)

### YAML_READER_ERROR = 2

Cannot read or decode the input stream.

[§](https://docs.rs#variant.YAML_SCANNER_ERROR)

### YAML_SCANNER_ERROR = 3

Cannot scan the input stream.

[§](https://docs.rs#variant.YAML_PARSER_ERROR)

### YAML_PARSER_ERROR = 4

Cannot parse the input stream.

[§](https://docs.rs#variant.YAML_COMPOSER_ERROR)

### YAML_COMPOSER_ERROR = 5

[§](https://docs.rs#variant.YAML_WRITER_ERROR)

### YAML_WRITER_ERROR = 6

[§](https://docs.rs#variant.YAML_EMITTER_ERROR)

### YAML_EMITTER_ERROR = 7

Cannot emit a YAML stream.

# yaml_document_get_root_node in unsafe_libyaml_norway - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/unsafe-libyaml-norway/0.2.15/unsafe_libyaml_norway/fn.yaml_document_get_root_node.html

```
pub unsafe fn yaml_document_get_root_node(
    document:
```
[*mut ](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/primitive.pointer.html)[yaml_document_t](https://docs.rs/struct.yaml_document_t.html),
) -> [*mut ](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/primitive.pointer.html)[yaml_node_t](https://docs.rs/struct.yaml_node_t.html)## Expand description

Get the root of a YAML document node.

The root object is the first object added to the document.

The pointer returned by this function is valid until any of the functions modifying the documents are called.

An empty document produced by the parser signifies the end of a YAML stream.

Returns the node object or NULL if the document is empty.

---

# yaml_emitter_dump in unsafe_libyaml_norway - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/unsafe-libyaml-norway/0.2.15/unsafe_libyaml_norway/fn.yaml_emitter_dump.html

```
pub unsafe fn yaml_emitter_dump(
    emitter:
```
[*mut ](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/primitive.pointer.html)[yaml_emitter_t](https://docs.rs/struct.yaml_emitter_t.html),
    document: [*mut ](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/primitive.pointer.html)[yaml_document_t](https://docs.rs/struct.yaml_document_t.html),
) -> Success## Expand description

Emit a YAML document.

The document object may be generated using the yaml_parser_load() function or the yaml_document_initialize() function. The emitter takes the responsibility for the document object and destroys its content after it is emitted. The document object is destroyed even if the function fails.

# yaml_emitter_set_output_string in unsafe_libyaml_norway - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/unsafe-libyaml-norway/0.2.15/unsafe_libyaml_norway/fn.yaml_emitter_set_output_string.html

```
pub unsafe fn yaml_emitter_set_output_string(
    emitter:
```
[*mut ](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/primitive.pointer.html)[yaml_emitter_t](https://docs.rs/struct.yaml_emitter_t.html),
    output: [*mut ](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/primitive.pointer.html)[u8](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/primitive.u8.html),
    size: [u64](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/primitive.u64.html),

)## Expand description

Set a string output.

The emitter will write the output characters to the `output` buffer of the
size `size`. The emitter will set `size_written` to the number of written
bytes. If the buffer is smaller than required, the emitter produces the
YAML_WRITE_ERROR error.

# yaml_parser_load in unsafe_libyaml_norway - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/unsafe-libyaml-norway/0.2.15/unsafe_libyaml_norway/fn.yaml_parser_load.html

```
pub unsafe fn yaml_parser_load(
    parser:
```
[*mut ](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/primitive.pointer.html)[yaml_parser_t](https://docs.rs/struct.yaml_parser_t.html),
    document: [*mut ](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/primitive.pointer.html)[yaml_document_t](https://docs.rs/struct.yaml_document_t.html),
) -> Success## Expand description

Parse the input stream and produce the next YAML document.

Call this function subsequently to produce a sequence of documents constituting the input stream.

If the produced document has no root node, it means that the document end has been reached.

An application is responsible for freeing any data associated with the produced document object using the yaml_document_delete() function.

An application must not alternate the calls of yaml_parser_load() with the calls of yaml_parser_scan() or yaml_parser_parse(). Doing this will break the parser.

---

# yaml_parser_parse in unsafe_libyaml_norway - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/unsafe-libyaml-norway/0.2.15/unsafe_libyaml_norway/fn.yaml_parser_parse.html

```
pub unsafe fn yaml_parser_parse(
    parser:
```
[*mut ](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/primitive.pointer.html)[yaml_parser_t](https://docs.rs/struct.yaml_parser_t.html),
    event: [*mut ](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/primitive.pointer.html)[yaml_event_t](https://docs.rs/struct.yaml_event_t.html),
) -> Success## Expand description

Parse the input stream and produce the next parsing event.

Call the function subsequently to produce a sequence of events corresponding to the input stream. The initial event has the type YAML_STREAM_START_EVENT while the ending event has the type YAML_STREAM_END_EVENT.

An application is responsible for freeing any buffers associated with the produced event object using the yaml_event_delete() function.

An application must not alternate the calls of yaml_parser_parse() with the calls of yaml_parser_scan() or yaml_parser_load(). Doing this will break the parser.

---

# yaml_parser_scan in unsafe_libyaml_norway - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/unsafe-libyaml-norway/0.2.15/unsafe_libyaml_norway/fn.yaml_parser_scan.html

```
pub unsafe fn yaml_parser_scan(
    parser:
```
[*mut ](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/primitive.pointer.html)[yaml_parser_t](https://docs.rs/struct.yaml_parser_t.html),
    token: [*mut ](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/primitive.pointer.html)[yaml_token_t](https://docs.rs/struct.yaml_token_t.html),
) -> Success## Expand description

Scan the input stream and produce the next token.

Call the function subsequently to produce a sequence of tokens corresponding to the input stream. The initial token has the type YAML_STREAM_START_TOKEN while the ending token has the type YAML_STREAM_END_TOKEN.

An application is responsible for freeing any buffers associated with the produced token object using the yaml_token_delete function.

An application must not alternate the calls of yaml_parser_scan() with the calls of yaml_parser_parse() or yaml_parser_load(). Doing this will break the parser.

---

# yaml_read_handler_t in unsafe_libyaml_norway - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/unsafe-libyaml-norway/0.2.15/unsafe_libyaml_norway/type.yaml_read_handler_t.html

`pub type yaml_read_handler_t = unsafe `[fn](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/primitive.fn.html)(data: [*mut ](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/primitive.pointer.html)[c_void](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/ffi/enum.c_void.html), buffer: [*mut ](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/primitive.pointer.html)[u8](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/primitive.u8.html), size: [u64](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/primitive.u64.html), size_read: [*mut ](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/primitive.pointer.html)[u64](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/primitive.u64.html)) -> [i32](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/primitive.i32.html);## Expand description

The prototype of a read handler.

The read handler is called when the parser needs to read more bytes from the
source. The handler should write not more than `size` bytes to the `buffer`.
The number of written bytes should be set to the `length` variable.

On success, the handler should return 1. If the handler failed, the returned
value should be 0. On EOF, the handler should set the `size_read` to 0 and
return 1.

---

# yaml_write_handler_t in unsafe_libyaml_norway - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/unsafe-libyaml-norway/0.2.15/unsafe_libyaml_norway/type.yaml_write_handler_t.html

## Expand description

The prototype of a write handler.

The write handler is called when the emitter needs to flush the accumulated
characters to the output. The handler should write `size` bytes of the
`buffer` to the output.

On success, the handler should return 1. If the handler failed, the returned value should be 0.

---

- Finish a YAML stream.
- [yaml_](https://docs.rs/fn.yaml_emitter_delete.html)- emitter_ - delete - ⚠
- Destroy an emitter.
- [yaml_](https://docs.rs/fn.yaml_emitter_dump.html)- emitter_ - dump - ⚠
- Emit a YAML document.
- [yaml_](https://docs.rs/fn.yaml_emitter_emit.html)- emitter_ - emit - ⚠
- Emit an event.
- [yaml_](https://docs.rs/fn.yaml_emitter_flush.html)- emitter_ - flush - ⚠
- Flush the accumulated characters to the output.
- [yaml_](https://docs.rs/fn.yaml_emitter_initialize.html)- emitter_ - initialize - ⚠
- Initialize an emitter.
- [yaml_](https://docs.rs/fn.yaml_emitter_open.html)- emitter_ - open - ⚠
- Start a YAML stream.
- [yaml_](https://docs.rs/fn.yaml_emitter_set_break.html)- emitter_ - set_ - break - ⚠
- Set the preferred line break.
- [yaml_](https://docs.rs/fn.yaml_emitter_set_canonical.html)- emitter_ - set_ - canonical - ⚠
- Set if the output should be in the “canonical” format as in the YAML specification.
- [yaml_](https://docs.rs/fn.yaml_emitter_set_encoding.html)- emitter_ - set_ - encoding - ⚠
- Set the output encoding.
- [yaml_](https://docs.rs/fn.yaml_emitter_set_indent.html)- emitter_ - set_ - indent - ⚠
- Set the indentation increment.
- [yaml_](https://docs.rs/fn.yaml_emitter_set_output.html)- emitter_ - set_ - output - ⚠
- Set a generic output handler.
- [yaml_](https://docs.rs/fn.yaml_emitter_set_output_string.html)- emitter_ - set_ - output_ - string - ⚠
- Set a string output.
- [yaml_](https://docs.rs/fn.yaml_emitter_set_unicode.html)- emitter_ - set_ - unicode - ⚠
- Set if unescaped non-ASCII characters are allowed.
- [yaml_](https://docs.rs/fn.yaml_emitter_set_width.html)- emitter_ - set_ - width - ⚠
- Set the preferred line width. -1 means unlimited.
- [yaml_](https://docs.rs/fn.yaml_event_delete.html)- event_ - delete - ⚠
- Free any memory allocated for an event object.
- [yaml_](https://docs.rs/fn.yaml_mapping_end_event_initialize.html)- mapping_ - end_ - event_ - initialize - ⚠
- Create a MAPPING-END event.
- [yaml_](https://docs.rs/fn.yaml_mapping_start_event_initialize.html)- mapping_ - start_ - event_ - initialize - ⚠
- Create a MAPPING-START event.
- [yaml_](https://docs.rs/fn.yaml_parser_delete.html)- parser_ - delete - ⚠
- Destroy a parser.
- [yaml_](https://docs.rs/fn.yaml_parser_initialize.html)- parser_ - initialize - ⚠
- Initialize a parser.
- [yaml_](https://docs.rs/fn.yaml_parser_load.html)- parser_ - load - ⚠
- Parse the input stream and produce the next YAML document.
- [yaml_](https://docs.rs/fn.yaml_parser_parse.html)- parser_ - parse - ⚠
- Parse the input stream and produce the next parsing event.
- [yaml_](https://docs.rs/fn.yaml_parser_scan.html)- parser_ - scan - ⚠
- Scan the input stream and produce the next token.
- [yaml_](https://docs.rs/fn.yaml_parser_set_encoding.html)- parser_ - set_ - encoding - ⚠
- Set the source encoding.
- [yaml_](https://docs.rs/fn.yaml_parser_set_input.html)- parser_ - set_ - input - ⚠
- Set a generic input handler.
- [yaml_](https://docs.rs/fn.yaml_parser_set_input_string.html)- parser_ - set_ - input_ - string - ⚠
- Set a string input.
- [yaml_](https://docs.rs/fn.yaml_scalar_event_initialize.html)- scalar_ - event_ - initialize - ⚠
- Create a SCALAR event.
- [yaml_](https://docs.rs/fn.yaml_sequence_end_event_initialize.html)- sequence_ - end_ - event_ - initialize - ⚠
- Create a SEQUENCE-END event.
- [yaml_](https://docs.rs/fn.yaml_sequence_start_event_initialize.html)- sequence_ - start_ - event_ - initialize - ⚠
- Create a SEQUENCE-START event.
- [yaml_](https://docs.rs/fn.yaml_stream_end_event_initialize.html)- stream_ - end_ - event_ - initialize - ⚠
- Create the STREAM-END event.
- [yaml_](https://docs.rs/fn.yaml_stream_start_event_initialize.html)- stream_ - start_ - event_ - initialize - ⚠
- Create the STREAM-START event.
- [yaml_](https://docs.rs/fn.yaml_token_delete.html)- token_ - delete - ⚠
- Free any memory allocated for a token object.

## Type Aliases[§](https://docs.rs#types)

- [yaml_](https://docs.rs/type.yaml_node_item_t.html)- node_ - item_ - t
- An element of a sequence node.
- [yaml_](https://docs.rs/type.yaml_read_handler_t.html)- read_ - handler_ - t
- The prototype of a read handler.
- [yaml_](https://docs.rs/type.yaml_write_handler_t.html)- write_ - handler_ - t
- The prototype of a write handler.

# unsafe-libyaml-norway 0.2.15 - Docs.rs

Source: https://docs.rs/crate/unsafe-libyaml-norway/latest/builds

All the builds on docs.rs are executed inside a sandbox with limited resources. The limits for this crate are the following:

| Available RAM | 6.44 GB |
| Maximum rustdoc execution time | 15m |
| Maximum size of a build log | 102.4 kB |
| Network access | blocked |
| Maximum number of build targets | 10 |

                    If a build fails because it hit one of those limits please
                    [open an issue](https://github.com/rust-lang/docs.rs/issues/new/choose)
                    to get them increased.

# pretty_assertions 1.4.1 - Docs.rs

Source: https://docs.rs/crate/pretty_assertions/^1.0

# Pretty Assertions

Overwrite `assert_eq!` with a drop-in replacement, adding a colorful diff.

## Usage

When writing tests in Rust, you'll probably use `assert_eq!(a, b)` *a lot*.

If such a test fails, it will present all the details of `a` and `b`.
But you have to spot the differences yourself, which is not always straightforward,
like here:

Wouldn't that task be *much* easier with a colorful diff?

Yep — and you only need **one line of code** to make it happen:

```
use ;
```
```
// 1. add the `pretty_assertions` dependency to `Cargo.toml`.
// 2. insert this line at the top of each module, as needed
use ;
```
## Semantic Versioning

The exact output of assertions is **not guaranteed** to be consistent over time, and may change between minor versions.
The output of this crate is designed to be read by a human. It is not suitable for exact comparison, for example in snapshot testing.

This crate adheres to semantic versioning for publically exported crate items, **except** the `private` module, which may change between any version.

## Tip

Specify it as [ [dev-dependencies]](http://doc.crates.io/specifying-dependencies.html#development-dependencies)
and it will only be used for compiling tests, examples, and benchmarks.
This way the compile time of

`cargo build` won't be affected!Also add `#[cfg(test)]` to your `use` statements, like this:

```
use ;
```
## Notes

- Since `Rust 2018`edition, you need to declare`use pretty_assertions::{assert_eq, assert_ne};`per module. Before you would write`#[macro_use] extern crate pretty_assertions;`.
- The replacement is only effective in your own crate, not in other libraries you include.
- `assert_ne`is also switched to multi-line presentation, but does- *not*show a diff.
- Under Windows, the terminal state is modified to properly handle VT100 escape sequences, which may break display for certain use cases.
- The minimum supported rust version (MSRV) is 1.35.0

`no_std` support

For `no_std` support, disable the `std` feature and enable the `alloc` feature:

```
# Cargo.toml
 = { = "...",  = false,  = ["alloc"] }
```

- MIT license ([LICENSE-MIT](https://docs.rs/LICENSE-MIT)or[http://opensource.org/licenses/MIT](http://opensource.org/licenses/MIT))

at your option.

# unsafe-libyaml-norway

This library is [libyaml](https://github.com/yaml/libyaml/tree/2c891fc7a770e8ba2fec34fc6b545c672beb37e6) translated from C to unsafe Rust with the assistance
of [c2rust](https://github.com/immunant/c2rust).

[]
 = "0.2"
```
*Compiler support: requires rustc 1.60+*

# unsafe-libyaml-norway 0.2.15 - Docs.rs

Source: https://docs.rs/crate/unsafe-libyaml-norway/latest/source/flake.nix

```
{
  inputs = {
    nixpkgs.url = "github:NixOS/nixpkgs/nixpkgs-unstable";
    crane = {
      url = "github:ipetkov/crane";
      inputs.nixpkgs.follows = "nixpkgs";
    };
    fenix = {
      url = "github:nix-community/fenix";
      inputs.nixpkgs.follows = "nixpkgs";
      inputs.rust-analyzer-src.follows = "";
    };
    flake-utils.url = "github:numtide/flake-utils";
    rust-overlay = {
      url = "github:oxalica/rust-overlay";
      inputs = {
        nixpkgs.follows = "nixpkgs";
      };
    };
    advisory-db = {
      url = "github:rustsec/advisory-db";
      flake = false;
    };
  };
  outputs =
    {
      self,
      nixpkgs,
      crane,
      fenix,
      flake-utils,
      advisory-db,
      rust-overlay,
      ...
    }:
    flake-utils.lib.eachDefaultSystem (
      system:
      let
        overlays = [ (import rust-overlay) ];
        pkgs = (import nixpkgs) { inherit system overlays; };
        inherit (pkgs) lib;
        toolchain = pkgs.rust-bin.fromRustupToolchainFile ./.config/rust-toolchain.toml;
        craneLib = (crane.mkLib pkgs).overrideToolchain toolchain;
        src = craneLib.cleanCargoSource (craneLib.path ./.);
        # Common arguments can be set here to avoid repeating them later
        commonArgs = {
          inherit src;
          strictDeps = true;
          buildInputs =
            [
              # Add additional build inputs here
            ]
            ++ lib.optionals pkgs.stdenv.isDarwin [
              # Additional darwin specific inputs can be set here
              pkgs.libiconv
            ];
          # Additional environment variables can be set directly
          # MY_CUSTOM_VAR = "some value";
        };
        craneLibLLvmTools = craneLib.overrideToolchain (
          fenix.packages.${system}.complete.withComponents [
            "cargo"
            "llvm-tools"
            "rustc"
          ]
        );
        # Build *just* the cargo dependencies, so we can reuse
        # all of that work (e.g. via cachix) when running in CI
        cargoArtifacts = craneLib.buildDepsOnly commonArgs;
        # Build the actual crate itself, reusing the dependency
        # artifacts from above.
        unsafe-libyaml = craneLib.buildPackage (
          commonArgs
          // {
            inherit cargoArtifacts;
          }
        );
      in
      {
        checks = {
          # Build the crate as part of `nix flake check` for convenience
          inherit unsafe-libyaml;
          # Run clippy (and deny all warnings) on the crate source,
          # again, reusing the dependency artifacts from above.
          #
          # Note that this is done as a separate derivation so that
          # we can block the CI if there are issues here, but not
          # prevent downstream consumers from building our crate by itself.
          unsafe-libyaml-clippy = craneLib.cargoClippy (
            commonArgs
            // {
              inherit cargoArtifacts;
              cargoClippyExtraArgs = "--all-targets -- --deny warnings -Dclippy::all -Dclippy::pedantic";
            }
          );
          unsafe-libyaml-doc = craneLib.cargoDoc (
            commonArgs
            // {
              inherit cargoArtifacts;
            }
          );
          # Check formatting
          unsafe-libyaml-fmt = craneLib.cargoFmt {
            inherit src;
          };
          # Audit dependencies
          unsafe-libyaml-audit = craneLib.cargoAudit {
            inherit src advisory-db;
          };
          # Audit licenses
          unsafe-libyaml-deny = craneLib.cargoDeny {
            inherit src;
          };
          # Run tests with cargo-nextest
          # Consider setting `doCheck = false` on `unsafe-libyaml` if you do not want
          # the tests to run twice
          unsafe-libyaml-nextest = craneLib.cargoNextest (
            commonArgs
            // {
              inherit cargoArtifacts;
              partitions = 1;
              partitionType = "count";
            }
          );
        };
        packages =
          {
            default = unsafe-libyaml;
          }
          // lib.optionalAttrs (!pkgs.stdenv.isDarwin) {
            unsafe-libyaml-llvm-coverage = craneLibLLvmTools.cargoLlvmCov (
              commonArgs
              // {
                inherit cargoArtifacts;
              }
            );
          };
        apps.default = flake-utils.lib.mkApp {
          drv = unsafe-libyaml;
        };
        devShells.default = craneLib.devShell {
          # Inherit inputs from checks.
          checks = self.checks.${system};
          # Additional dev-shell environment variables can be set directly
          # MY_CUSTOM_DEVELOPMENT_VAR = "something else";
          # Extra inputs can be added here; cargo and rustc are provided by default.
          packages = [
            pkgs.cargo-outdated
            pkgs.pkg-config
            pkgs.openssl
          ];
        };
      }
    );
}
```

# pretty_assertions 1.4.1 - Docs.rs

Source: https://docs.rs/crate/pretty_assertions/1.4.1

# Pretty Assertions

Overwrite `assert_eq!` with a drop-in replacement, adding a colorful diff.

## Usage

When writing tests in Rust, you'll probably use `assert_eq!(a, b)` *a lot*.

If such a test fails, it will present all the details of `a` and `b`.
But you have to spot the differences yourself, which is not always straightforward,
like here:

Wouldn't that task be *much* easier with a colorful diff?

Yep — and you only need **one line of code** to make it happen:

```
use ;
```
```
// 1. add the `pretty_assertions` dependency to `Cargo.toml`.
// 2. insert this line at the top of each module, as needed
use ;
```
## Semantic Versioning

The exact output of assertions is **not guaranteed** to be consistent over time, and may change between minor versions.
The output of this crate is designed to be read by a human. It is not suitable for exact comparison, for example in snapshot testing.

This crate adheres to semantic versioning for publically exported crate items, **except** the `private` module, which may change between any version.

## Tip

Specify it as [ [dev-dependencies]](http://doc.crates.io/specifying-dependencies.html#development-dependencies)
and it will only be used for compiling tests, examples, and benchmarks.
This way the compile time of

`cargo build` won't be affected!Also add `#[cfg(test)]` to your `use` statements, like this:

```
use ;
```
## Notes

- Since `Rust 2018`edition, you need to declare`use pretty_assertions::{assert_eq, assert_ne};`per module. Before you would write`#[macro_use] extern crate pretty_assertions;`.
- The replacement is only effective in your own crate, not in other libraries you include.
- `assert_ne`is also switched to multi-line presentation, but does- *not*show a diff.
- Under Windows, the terminal state is modified to properly handle VT100 escape sequences, which may break display for certain use cases.
- The minimum supported rust version (MSRV) is 1.35.0

`no_std` support

For `no_std` support, disable the `std` feature and enable the `alloc` feature:

```
# Cargo.toml
 = { = "...",  = false,  = ["alloc"] }
```

- MIT license ([LICENSE-MIT](https://docs.rs/LICENSE-MIT)or[http://opensource.org/licenses/MIT](http://opensource.org/licenses/MIT))

at your option.

# yansi - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/yansi/^1.0.1/

## Expand description

A dead simple ANSI terminal color painting library.

[§](https://docs.rs#features)Features

Why *y*et another *ANSI* terminal coloring library? Here are some reasons:

- This library makes simple things *simple*:`use``Paint`
- Zero dependencies by default. It really is simple.
- Zero allocations except as needed by opt-in [wrapping](https://docs.rs#wrapping).
- [Automatic Windows support](https://docs.rs#windows)for the vast majority (95%+) of Windows users.
- [Featureful](https://docs.rs#crate-features), no-- `no_std`- `alloc`, support with- `default-features = false`.
- `Style`constructors are- `const`
- *Any*type implementing a formatting trait can be styled, not just strings.
- Styling can be [enabled](https://docs.rs/fn.enable.html)and[disabled](https://docs.rs/fn.disable.html)globally and[dynamically](https://docs.rs/fn.whenever.html), on the fly.
- A `Style`can be predicated on arbitrary[conditions](https://docs.rs#per-style).
- Formatting specifiers like `{:x}`and`{:08b}`are supported and preserved!
- [Built-in (optional) conditions](https://docs.rs/struct.Condition.html#built-in-conditions)for- [TTY detection](https://docs.rs/struct.Condition.html#impl-Condition-1)and- [common environment variables](https://docs.rs/struct.Condition.html#impl-Condition-2).
- Arbitrary items can be *masked*
- Styling can *wrap*
- Styling can *linger*
- Experimental support for [hyperlinking](https://docs.rs/hyperlink/index.html)is included.
- The name `yansi`is pretty cool 😎.

All that said, `yansi` borrows API ideas from older libraries as well as
implementation details from [ ansi_term](https://crates.io/crates/ansi_term).

[§](https://docs.rs#usage)Usage

The [ Paint](https://docs.rs/trait.Paint.html) trait is implemented for every type. Import it and call
chainable builder methods:

```
use yansi::Paint;
println!("Testing, {}, {}, {}!",
    "Ready".bold(),
    "Set".yellow().italic(),
    "STOP".white().on_red().bright().underline().bold());
```
`>` Testing,
**Ready**,
* Set*,

__!__

**STOP**The methods return a [ Painted](https://docs.rs/struct.Painted.html) type which consists of a

[and a reference to the receiver. Displaying a](https://docs.rs/struct.Style.html)

`Style`[(via](https://docs.rs/struct.Painted.html)

`Painted``print!()`,
`format!()`, etc) results in emitting ANSI escape codes that effectuate the
style.[§](https://docs.rs#uniform-const-builders)Uniform `const` Builders

All builder methods are uniformly available for [ Style](https://docs.rs/struct.Style.html),

[, and](https://docs.rs/enum.Color.html)

`Color`[, which means you can chain calls across library types. All methods are](https://docs.rs/struct.Painted.html)

`Painted``const`, allowing creations of `const` or `static` [s. A](https://docs.rs/struct.Style.html)

`Style``Style` can be directly applied to values with [, from](https://docs.rs/trait.Paint.html#method.paint)

`.paint()`[, available for every type:](https://docs.rs/trait.Paint.html#method.paint)

`Paint::paint()````
use yansi::{Paint, Style, Color::*};
// `const` constructors allow static `Style`s for easy reuse
static ALERT: Style = White.bright().underline().italic().on_red();
println!("Testing, {}, {}, {}!",
    "Ready".bold(),
    "Set".yellow().bold(),
    "STOP".paint(ALERT));
```
`>` Testing,
**Ready**,
**Set**,
__ STOP__!

[§](https://docs.rs#conditional-styling)Conditional Styling

[§](https://docs.rs#globally)Globally

Styling is enabled by default but can be enabled and disabled globally via
[ enable()](https://docs.rs/fn.enable.html) and

[. When styling is disabled, no ANSI escape codes are emitted, and](https://docs.rs/fn.disable.html)

`disable()`[values are omitted entirely.](https://docs.rs#masking)

*masked*Global styling can also be dynamically enabled and disabled using
[ whenever()](https://docs.rs/fn.whenever.html) with an arbitrary

[: a function that returns](https://docs.rs/struct.Condition.html)

`Condition``true` or `false`. This condition is evaluated each time a [item is displayed. The associated styling is enabled, and mask values emitted, exactly when and only when the condition returns](https://docs.rs/struct.Painted.html)

`Painted``true`.[§](https://docs.rs#per-style)Per-`Style`

A specific `Style` can itself be conditionally applied by using
[ .whenever()](https://docs.rs/struct.Style.html#method.whenever):

```
use yansi::{Paint, Style, Color::*, Condition};
static WARNING: Style = Black.bold().on_yellow().whenever(Condition::STDERR_IS_TTY);
eprintln!("{}", "Bees can sting!".paint(WARNING));
```
With the above, if `stderr` is a TTY, then:
`>` **Bees can sting!**

If it is not a TTY, styling is not emitted:
`>` Bees can sting!

See [ Condition](https://docs.rs/struct.Condition.html) for a list of built-in conditions which require enabling
crate features.

[§](https://docs.rs#quirks)Quirks

As a convenience, `yansi` implements several “quirks”, applicable via
[ Quirk](https://docs.rs/enum.Quirk.html) and the respective methods, that modify if and how styling is
presented to the terminal. These quirks do not correspond to any ANSI
styling sequences.

[§](https://docs.rs#masking)Masking

Items can be arbitrarily *masked* with the [ mask()](https://docs.rs/trait.Paint.html#tymethod.mask) builder
method. Masked values are not emitted when styling is disabled, globally or
for a given style. This allows selective output based on whether styling is
enabled.

One use for this feature is to print certain characters only when styling is enabled. For instance, you might wish to emit the 🎨 emoji when coloring is enabled but not otherwise. This can be accomplished by masking the emoji:

```
use yansi::Paint;
println!("I like colors!{}", " 🎨".mask());
```
When styling is enabled, this prints: `>` I like colors! 🎨

With styling disabled, this prints: `>` I like colors!

[§](https://docs.rs#wrapping)Wrapping

**Note:** *Either the  std or alloc feature is required for wrapping.
std is enabled by default. See *

[crate features](https://docs.rs#crate-features).

Styling can *wrap* via [ Quirk::Wrap](https://docs.rs/enum.Quirk.html#variant.Wrap) or the equivalent

[constructor. A wrapping style modifies any styling resets emitted by the internal value so that they correspond to the wrapping style. In other words, the “reset” style of the wrapped item is modified to be the style being](https://docs.rs/struct.Painted.html#method.wrap)

`wrap()``.wrap()`d.Wrapping is useful in situations where opaque and arbitrary values must be styled consistently irrespective of any existing styling. For example, a generic logger might want to style messages based on log levels consistently, even when those messages may already include styling. Wrapping exists to enable such consistent styling:

```
use yansi::Paint;
// Imagine that `inner` is opaque and we don't know it's styling.
let inner = format!("{} and {}", "Stop".red(), "Go".green());
// We can use `wrap` to ensure anything in `inner` not styled is blue.
println!("Hey! {}", inner.blue().wrap());
```
Thanks to wrapping, this prints:
`>` Hey!
Stop and
Go

Without wrapping, the reset after `"Stop".red()` would not be overwritten:
`>` Hey! Stop and Go

Wrapping incurs a performance cost due to an extra allocation and replacement if the wrapped item has styling applied to it. Otherwise, it does not allocate nor incur a meaningful performance cost.

[§](https://docs.rs#lingering)Lingering

Styling can *linger* beyond a single value via [ Quirk::Linger](https://docs.rs/enum.Quirk.html#variant.Linger) or the
equivalent

[constructor. A lingering style does not reset itself after being applied. In other words, the style lingers on beyond the value it’s applied to, until something else resets the respective styling.](https://docs.rs/struct.Painted.html#method.linger)

`linger()`The complement to lingering is force resetting via [ Quirk::Resetting](https://docs.rs/enum.Quirk.html#variant.Resetting) or
the equivalent

[constructor. Force resetting, as the name implies, forces a reset suffix to be emitted after the value, irrespective of any lingering applied. It can be used as a way to finalize a lingering style.](https://docs.rs/struct.Painted.html#method.resetting)

`resetting()`Lingering itself is useful in situations where a given style is to be
repeated across multiple values, or when style is intended to persist even
across values that are not styled with `yansi`. It also allows avoiding
unnecessarily repeated ANSI code sequences. The examples below illustrate
some scenarios in which lingering is useful:

```
use yansi::Paint;
println!("Hello! {} {} things with {} {}?",
    "How".magenta().underline().linger(),
    "are".italic().linger(),
    "you".on_yellow(), // doesn't linger, so all styling is reset here
    "today".blue());
```
`>` Hello!
__How  are things with you__
today?

```
use yansi::Paint;
println!("Hello! {} {} things with {} {}?",
    "How".magenta().underline().linger(),
    "are".italic(), // doesn't linger, so all styling is reset here
    "you".on_yellow().linger(),
    "today".blue()); // doesn't linger; styling is reset
```
`>` Hello!
__How  are__
things with
you
today?

```
use yansi::Paint;
println!("{} B {} {} {} F",
    "A".red().linger(),
    "C".underline().linger(),
    "D", // doesn't linger, but no styling applied, thus no reset
    "E".resetting());  // explicitly reset
```
`>`  A B __C D E__  F

[§](https://docs.rs#brightening)Brightening

Most pimrary colors are available in regular and *bright* variants, e.g.,
[ Color::Red](https://docs.rs/enum.Color.html#variant.Red) and

[. The](https://docs.rs/enum.Color.html#variant.BrightRed)

`Color::BrightRed`[and](https://docs.rs/enum.Quirk.html#variant.Bright)

`Quirk::Bright`[quirks, typically applied via](https://docs.rs/enum.Quirk.html#variant.OnBright)

`Quirk::OnBright`[and](https://docs.rs/struct.Painted.html#method.bright)

`.bright()`[, provide an alternative, convenient mechanism to select the bright variant of the selected foreground or background color, respectively. The quirk provides no additional colors and is equivalent to selecting the bright variants directly.](https://docs.rs/struct.Painted.html#method.on_bright)

`.on_bright()````
use yansi::Paint;
// These are all equivalent.
print!("{}", "Regular".red());
print!("{}", "Bright".bright_red());
print!("{}", "Bright".bright().red());
print!("{}", "Bright".red().bright());
// The `bright` quirk lets use choose the bright variants of _any_ color,
// even when the color or style is unknown at the call site.
print!("{}", "Normal".paint(STYLE));
print!("{}", "Bright".paint(STYLE).bright());
```
`>` Regular
Bright
Bright
Bright
**Normal**
**Bright**

The `bright()` quirk can be applied before or after a color is selected
while having the same effect.

[§](https://docs.rs#windows)Windows

Styling is supported and enabled automatically on Windows beginning with
the Windows 10 Anniversary Update, or about [96% of all Windows machines
worldwide](https://gs.statcounter.com/os-version-market-share/windows/desktop/worldwide),
and likely closer to 100% of developer machines (e.g., 99% of visitors to
[rocket.rs](https://rocket.rs) on Windows are on Windows 10+).

Yansi enables styling support on Windows by querying the Windows API on the first attempt to color. If support is available, it is enabled. If support is not available, styling is disabled and no styling sequences are emitted.

[§](https://docs.rs#crate-features)Crate Features

| Feature | Default? | Also Enables | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| `std` | Y | `alloc` | Use `std`library. |
| `alloc` | Y | Use `alloc`. Enables[wrapping](https://docs.rs#wrapping). | |
| `detect-tty` | N | `std` | See [optional conditions](https://docs.rs/struct.Condition.html#built-in-conditions). |
| `detect-env` | N | `std` | See [optional conditions](https://docs.rs/struct.Condition.html#built-in-conditions). |
| `hyperlink` | N | `std` | Enables [hyperlinking](https://docs.rs/hyperlink/index.html)support. |

With `default-features = false`, this crate is `#[no_std]`.

Without any features enabled, all functionality except [wrapping](https://docs.rs#wrapping) is
available. To recover wrapping *with* `#[no_std]`, set `default-features = false` and enable the `alloc` feature, which requires `alloc` support.

# pretty_assertions - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/crate/pretty_assertions/1.4.1/target-redirect/pretty_assertions/

## Expand description

[§](https://docs.rs#pretty-assertions)Pretty Assertions

When writing tests in Rust, you’ll probably use `assert_eq!(a, b)` *a lot*.

If such a test fails, it will present all the details of `a` and `b`.
But you have to spot the differences yourself, which is not always straightforward,
like here:

Wouldn’t that task be *much* easier with a colorful diff?

Yep — and you only need **one line of code** to make it happen:

`use pretty_assertions::{assert_eq, assert_ne};`## Show the example behind the screenshots above.

[ⓘ](https://docs.rs)

```
// 1. add the `pretty_assertions` dependency to `Cargo.toml`.
// 2. insert this line at the top of each module, as needed
use pretty_assertions::{assert_eq, assert_ne};
#[derive(Debug, PartialEq)]
struct Foo {
    lorem: &'static str,
    ipsum: u32,
    dolor: Result<String, String>,
}
let x = Some(Foo { lorem: "Hello World!", ipsum: 42, dolor: Ok("hey".to_string())});
let y = Some(Foo { lorem: "Hello Wrold!", ipsum: 42, dolor: Ok("hey ho!".to_string())});
assert_eq!(x, y);
```
[§](https://docs.rs#tip)Tip

Specify it as [ [dev-dependencies]](http://doc.crates.io/specifying-dependencies.html#development-dependencies)
and it will only be used for compiling tests, examples, and benchmarks.
This way the compile time of

`cargo build` won’t be affected!Also add `#[cfg(test)]` to your `use` statements, like this:

```
#[cfg(test)]
use pretty_assertions::{assert_eq, assert_ne};
```
[§](https://docs.rs#note)Note

- Since `Rust 2018`edition, you need to declare`use pretty_assertions::{assert_eq, assert_ne};`per module. Before you would write`#[macro_use] extern crate pretty_assertions;`.
- The replacement is only effective in your own crate, not in other libraries you include.
- `assert_ne`is also switched to multi-line presentation, but does- *not*show a diff.

[§](https://docs.rs#features)Features

Features provided by the crate are:

- `std`: Use the Rust standard library. Enabled by default. Exactly one of- `std`and- `alloc`is required.
- `alloc`: Use the- `alloc`crate. Exactly one of- `std`and- `alloc`is required.
- `unstable`: opt-in to unstable features that may not follow Semantic Versioning. The implementation behind this feature is subject to change without warning between patch versions.

## Macros[§](https://docs.rs#macros)

- [assert_](https://docs.rs/macro.assert_eq.html)- eq
- Asserts that two expressions are equal to each other (using `PartialEq`
- [assert_](https://docs.rs/macro.assert_matches.html)- matches
- Asserts that a value matches a pattern.
- [assert_](https://docs.rs/macro.assert_ne.html)- ne
- Asserts that two expressions are not equal to each other (using `PartialEq`
- [assert_](https://docs.rs/macro.assert_str_eq.html)- str_ - eq
- Asserts that two expressions are equal to each other (using `PartialEq`

- [Comparison](https://docs.rs/struct.Comparison.html)

# assert_eq in pretty_assertions - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/pretty_assertions/^1.0/macro.assert_eq.html

```
macro_rules! assert_eq {
    ($left:expr, $right:expr$(,)?) => { ... };
    ($left:expr, $right:expr, $($arg:tt)*) => { ... };
    (@ $left:expr, $right:expr, $maybe_colon:expr, $($arg:tt)*) => { ... };
}
```
## Expand description

Asserts that two expressions are equal to each other (using [ PartialEq](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/cmp/trait.PartialEq.html)).

On panic, this macro will print a diff derived from [ Debug](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/fmt/trait.Debug.html) representation of
each value.

This is a drop in replacement for [ core::assert_eq!](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/macro.assert_eq.html).
You can provide a custom panic message if desired.

[§](https://docs.rs#examples)Examples

```
use pretty_assertions::assert_eq;
let a = 3;
let b = 1 + 2;
assert_eq!(a, b);
assert_eq!(a, b, "we are testing addition with {} and {}", a, b);
```

---

# assert_matches in pretty_assertions - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/pretty_assertions/^1.0/macro.assert_matches.html

```
macro_rules! assert_matches {
    ($left:expr, $( $pattern:pat )|+ $( if $guard: expr )? $(,)?) => { ... };
    ($left:expr, $( $pattern:pat )|+ $( if $guard: expr )?, $($arg:tt)+) => { ... };
    (@ $left:expr, $right:expr, $maybe_colon:expr, $($arg:tt)*) => { ... };
}
```
## Expand description

Asserts that a value matches a pattern.

On panic, this macro will print a diff derived from [ Debug](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/fmt/trait.Debug.html) representation of
the value, and a string representation of the pattern.

This is a drop in replacement for [`core::assert_matches::assert_matches!`].
You can provide a custom panic message if desired.

[§](https://docs.rs#examples)Examples

```
use pretty_assertions::assert_matches;
let a = Some(3);
assert_matches!(a, Some(_));
assert_matches!(a, Some(value) if value > 2, "we are testing {:?} with a pattern", a);
```
[§](https://docs.rs#features)Features

Requires the `unstable` feature to be enabled.

**Please note:** implementation under the `unstable` feature may be changed between
patch versions without warning.

---

# assert_ne in pretty_assertions - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/pretty_assertions/^1.0/macro.assert_ne.html

```
macro_rules! assert_ne {
    ($left:expr, $right:expr$(,)?) => { ... };
    ($left:expr, $right:expr, $($arg:tt)+) => { ... };
    (@ $left:expr, $right:expr, $maybe_colon:expr, $($arg:tt)+) => { ... };
}
```
## Expand description

Asserts that two expressions are not equal to each other (using [ PartialEq](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/cmp/trait.PartialEq.html)).

On panic, this macro will print the values of the expressions with their
[ Debug](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/fmt/trait.Debug.html) representations.

This is a drop in replacement for [ core::assert_ne!](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/macro.assert_ne.html).
You can provide a custom panic message if desired.

[§](https://docs.rs#examples)Examples

```
use pretty_assertions::assert_ne;
let a = 3;
let b = 2;
assert_ne!(a, b);
assert_ne!(a, b, "we are testing that the values are not equal");
```

---

# assert_str_eq in pretty_assertions - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/pretty_assertions/^1.0/macro.assert_str_eq.html

```
macro_rules! assert_str_eq {
    ($left:expr, $right:expr$(,)?) => { ... };
    ($left:expr, $right:expr, $($arg:tt)*) => { ... };
    (@ $left:expr, $right:expr, $maybe_colon:expr, $($arg:tt)*) => { ... };
}
```
## Expand description

Asserts that two expressions are equal to each other (using [ PartialEq](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/cmp/trait.PartialEq.html)).

On panic, this macro will print a diff derived from each value’s [ str](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.str.html) representation.
See

[for further details.](https://docs.rs/struct.StrComparison.html)

`StrComparison`This is a drop in replacement for [ core::assert_eq!](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/macro.assert_eq.html).
You can provide a custom panic message if desired.

[§](https://docs.rs#examples)Examples

```
use pretty_assertions::assert_str_eq;
let a = "foo\nbar";
let b = ["foo", "bar"].join("\n");
assert_str_eq!(a, b);
assert_str_eq!(a, b, "we are testing concatenation with {} and {}", a, b);
```
